International Settlement and the French Concession. 

About 200 followers of the locAl "national salvation" 
movement have been mobilized and formed into groups of 
from two to five persons each. Each group will visit various

当地“救国”运动的约200名追随者已被动员起来，编成每组二至五人的小组。每个小组将访问各种公共场所，包括弄堂、工厂、学校和娱乐场所，届时将向人们秘密分发与该运动有关的印刷品。这些人员还打算在情况允许时，向接受此类宣传的人解释该运动的性质。这种谨慎的原因当然是为了尽可能避免与当局发生摩擦，他们的目的是尽可能秘密地进行这些活动。

以下是为分发而准备的三种宣传品的译文（样本附后）：-

1) 一张题为“宣誓不做汉奸，并铲除汉奸”的纸片，内容如下：-

(a) 我决不当汉奸。

become traitors.

c) I will never allow traitors in my house.

d) I will do my best to annihilate traitors.
for the good of the nation.

2) A handbill entitled "Letter to Shanghai citizens in
connection with the movement to annihilate traitors,"
urging the people to take drastic measures against
traitors including unscrupulous merchants and to boycott
Japanese goods.

3) A paper slip containing a sketch describing a party of
persons chasing a traitor. It also contains the following
inscriptions in Chinese :-

a) Exterminate traitors!

b) Boycott Japanese goods!

c) Take action against traitorous merchants!

d) The people organize groups to exterminate traitors!

e) Take the oath not to become traitors!

To each group of propagandists has been issued a
copy of a guide to the movement, which contains the following
captions:-

1. The political meaning of the anti-traitor movement;

a) To antagonize the Chinese public against traitors
with the ultimate object of making use of the power
of the masses to suppress traitors.

b) To signify the protest of the Chinese public against
the attitude of the Settlement Authorities in suppres-
sing the national salvation movement.

c) To encourage the Shanghai masses to continue support
of the war of resistance, and to lay the foundation of
a scheme to organize the masses.

2. Principal instruction in the anti-traitor movement:

As the situation has changed since November 2, when a
"Defence of Greater Shanghai" movement was carried out,
it is now not necessary to launch a severe counter-attack

b) 我将劝告我的亲友不当汉奸。

c) 我决不允许汉奸进入我家。

以利于国家。

已向每组宣传员发放了一份运动指南，其中包含以下标题：-

1. 反汉奸运动的政治意义；

a) 激起中国公众对汉奸的敌意，最终目的是利用群众的力量镇压汉奸。

b) 表示中国公众对租界当局压制救国运动态度的抗议。

c) 鼓励上海民众继续支持抗战，并为组织群众的方案奠定基础。

2. 反汉奸运动的主要指示：

由于自11月2日开展“大上海防卫”运动以来局势已发生变化，现在没有必要对租界当局发动猛烈反击

campaign should be carried out in an individual form
and mass movements should be avoided. No propaganda
matter should be posted but should be handed to the
people by individuals. The campaign should be mild.

3. Methods of carrying out the campaign:-
Places: streets, alleyways, factories, schools, families,
amusement resorts, shops, etc.

Methods:-
a) Handing of propaganda matter to the people individually
and where possible, verbal explanation of the movement

b) Convening small discussion meetings of friends and

g) Mobilizing the masses to proceed to the neighbourhood

3. 开展运动的方法：-

h) 鼓励群众处置在街上发现的汉奸，特别是在难民聚集的地方。

With reference to the attached report on the anniversary
of the birthday of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen, which fell on
November 12: the manager of the Lyric Theatre, 780 Peking
Road, was warned by the Municipal Police on November 11 against
holding meetings of a political nature.
At about 9.50a.m., November 12, however, approximately
280 persons of the student type, despite attempts on the part
of the management to dissuade them, entered the Lyric Theatre,
780 Peking Road, and held a meeting under the leadership of
one Mr. Tsui Yau Tsung (朱效春), an executive member of the
local Tangpu. Mr. Tsui delivered a short speech on the life
of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen and urged the audience to struggle
hard for the existence of the nation. The audience then
remained silent for a few minutes as a mark of respect for the
deceased Kuomintang leader and those who were killed during
the Sino-Japanese hostilities. The meeting broke up at 10.15
am. with the audience singing the "Kuomintang song" and "March
of Volunteer Armies Song" and shouting the following three
slogans:-
"Long Live the Republic of China!"
"Overthrow Japanese Imperialism!"
"Carry on the War of Resistance to the bitter end!"

nicated with by telephone in the evening of November 9 and
requested to give more detail on the information contained in
his letter so that definite steps could be taken in preventing
any such occurrence but apart from admitting the writer of
the letter, Mr. Woo could throw no further light upon the
matter. He states that the information came from a member
of the association whose name he was unable to disclose, but
this informant had stated that it was the intention of these
unscrupulous persons to commit murder and stage riots leaving
clues behind that would point to the National Salvation

object of having all such associations closed.
Mr. Woo was asked if it was possible to find this person
and arrangements could be made to interview him secretly,

Between 11.10 a.m. and 1.20 p.m. November 5, detectives
attached to this Branch with the assistance of uniform and
detective personnel attached to Chengtu Road Station proceeded
to Rooms 519-522 Lootung Guild, 1454 Avenue Edward VII and
seized a quantity of books, papers, pamphlets, printing
paraphernalia, banners etc., the property of the Shanghai
Cultural Circles National Salvation Association, which was
subsequently brought to headquarters.

Mr. Ju Han(吴汉), responsible staff member of the
Association who was present during the police visit, and Mr.
Chang Tsz Kiang(張志讓), executive committee member of the
Association who was communicated with by telephone but who
refused to appear at the offices in person, were informed that
in view of the strong political nature of their activities and
their refusal to heed police warnings, that the Council had
decided to close their offices. It was explained to them
that the Council had no objection to the distribution of
comforts to wounded soldiers and relief work among refugees.

A list of the seized property is attached hereto.

The Shanghai Municipality Film Studio Owners
Association (上海市電影業業主公會) is also situated in the above
offices but as this organization is not of a radical or
otherwise objectionable nature the documents connected with
it were not disturbed and the staff were informed that they
would be able to carry on as usual.

Two C.P.C.s have been posted near the offices to
ensure that police instructions are observed by the staff of
the first mentioned organization.

necessary assistance when search of the above mentioned

sever diplomatic relations with Japan.

the signatories of the Nine Power Treaty requesting

participate in the forthcoming conference of the
signatories of the Nine Power Treaty be made.
f) That propaganda for the severance of diplomatic
relations with Japan be carried out commencing
from October 26 for one week.
g) That each organization represented be asked to
post 500 posters bearing slogans on every day
of the Propaganda Week.
h) That an oath taking ceremony to have no further
relations with Japan be held on October 29.

Subject National Salvation Workers Training Institute - new organization formed.
Made by Clerk Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C. G...

A "National Salvation Workers Training Institute" has recently come into existence with an office at Room No.522 Pootung Guild, No.1454 Avenue Edward VII. This Institute was organized by the Shanghai Cultural Circles Race Salvation Association and claims as its object the training of enthusiastic and patriotic youths in order to prepare them to work in extending the people's movement for national salvation during the war period.

On September 26, 1937, the institute began to enrol students and to date a total of some 400 persons, most of whom are senior middle school students, have applied for registration. An entrance examination will be held on October 3, 1937 and out of the 400 registered 100 will be selected to sit this examination.

According to the regulations of the Institute the course should be completed in one month and the students while undergoing this training will be required to reside on the premises. On graduation, they will be sent to various places to be allotted by the institute, for the conducting of work in connection with the people's movement. No tuition fee will be collected but students are required to pay $6 towards the expenses for meals.

Mr. Zien Ching Zueh (钱俊瑞), Chief of the Propaganda Department of the Shanghai Cultural Circles Race Salvation Association, is in charge of this Institute.

The following documents together with translations are attached to this report:

September 16, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

SIXTH ANNIVERSARY OF SEPTEMBER 18 TO BE COMMEMORATED

The sixth anniversary of the September 18 Incident is soon approaching. In accordance with the rules laid down by the National Government, the local Tangpu Headquarters have decided upon the following arrangements for the commemoration of this anniversary:-
(1) National Flag to be hoisted at half mast throughout Shanghai.
(2) All local residents to observe a vegetable diet on the day and to contribute the proceeds thus saved for the comfort of the fighting troops.
(3) To promote the consumption of "Kwang" (Glory) cakes instead of moon cakes. It may be recalled that these "Kwang" cakes were used as provisions for the troops under the command of General Tsi Chi-kwang of the now defunct Ming Dynasty, who were then engaged in an expeditionary campaign against an invasion by the dwarf bandits. The local foodstuff shops have been notified by the Chamber of Commerce to redouble their efforts in the production of such cakes so as to meet local requirements.
(4) Local residents to observe a 3-minute silence at 12 noon on September 18.
(5) To promote a spiritual movement for national defence along the following lines:-
a) To denounce as traitors all those who spoil the unified and nation-wide resistance against the enemy at this time of resistance.
b) To denounce as non-citizens of the Chinese Republic all those who refuse to contribute either human labour or the wealth which they possess.

August 1, 1937. Morning Translation

National Herald and other local newspapers :-

MEETING OF THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE OF THE SHANGHAI CULTURAL
CIRCLES' NATIONAL EXTINCTION AVERSION ASSOCIATION

The Executive Committee of the Shanghai Cultural
Circles' National Extinction Aversion Association held its
first meeting at 6 p.m. July 30 at the Ih Kyia Tsung (一家春)
Restaurant. About 50 members including Messrs. Pan Kung-chan,
Nyien Ngoh-sung (嚴諤聲), Sa Kung-liao (薩空了), Dao Pah-
chuen (陶百川), Wu Kai-sien (吳開先), Chow Chien-yuin (周劍云)
and Chang Ts-niang (張資平) were present. Mr. Pan Kung-chan
presided.

Mr. Pan Kung-chan delivered a lengthy speech in the
course of which he exhorted the people in various walks of life
throughout the country to have implicit confidence in their
leader and government who had already made up their minds to
fight out of the present crisis. Continuing, Mr. Pan said:-
"We cannot put up a fight unless our views and spirit are
uniform. The defeat of the 29th Army is on the one hand
glorious but on the other a sad one. The defeat is attributable
to non-uniformity in spirit and views. The enemy is employing
the tactics of creating dissension between the Central Govern-
ment and the 29th Army and among the officers and men of the
29th Army. As a result, the views and spirit of the senior
officers of the 29th Army are not harmonious; some advocate
peace while others favour war. We must follow in the steps
of Turkey and have implicit confidence in General Chiang Kai-
shek as the leader of the united war of resistance and obey
his instructions. If we do this, China's revival is assured."
The following resolutions were then discussed and
passed :-
(1) That Messrs. Pan Kung-chan, Chow Chien-yuin,
Chang Ts-niang, Chow Han-mei (周寒梅), Zia Loh-yih (謝六逸),
Sung Dzu-chiu (沈茲九), Dao Pah-chuen, Sa Kung-liao, Koo Chih-
tsong (顧執中), Tsai Tsoo-sung (蔡楚生), Eu-Yang Yu-chi
(歐陽予倩), Chu Tsing-lai (諸青來), Yih Ling-voong (葉靈鳳)
and Zien Tsing-zai (錢俊瑞) be appointed standing members of
the Executive Committee.
(2) That the Shanghai Municipality Various Circles'
Enemy-Resisting Support Committee be requested by letter to
enforce a drastic boycott of "inferior" goods, to assist the
government in the tightening of smuggling preventive work, and
to start a movement for the manufacture of 100,000 gas masks.
(3) That a citizens' mass meeting be convened in a
week's time.
(4) That the Central Publicity Department of the
Kuomintang be requested to encourage the publication of
patriotic speeches.
(5) That groups to render service in the war area
in the North be organized.
(6) That various local dramatic groups be invited
to stage a joint performance for the purpose of raising a fund
for the comfort of the officers and men resisting the enemy.
(7) That various local cultural bodies be invited
to undertake extensive propaganda.

《国民新闻报》及其他本地报纸：-

上海文化界救亡协会执行委员会会议

上海文化界救亡协会执行委员会于7月30日下午6时在一家春餐厅举行了第一次会议。潘公展、嚴諤聲、薩空了、陶百川、吳開先、周劍云和張資平等约50名成员出席。潘公展先生主持。

潘公展先生发表了长篇演讲，期间他敦促全国各界人士对已下定决心摆脱当前危机的领袖和政府抱有信心。潘先生接着说：“除非我们的观点和精神统一，否则我们无法进行战斗。第29军的失败一方面是光荣的，但另一方面也是悲惨的。失败归因于精神和观点的不统一。敌人正在利用制造中央政府与第29军之间以及第29军官兵之间分歧的策略。结果，第29军高级军官的观点和精神不和谐；有些人主张和平，而其他人赞成战争。我们必须效仿土耳其，对作为联合抗战领袖的蒋介石将军抱有信心，并服从他的指示。如果我们这样做，中国的复兴就有保障了。”
随后讨论并通过了以下决议：-
(1) 任命潘公展、周劍云、張資平、周寒梅、謝六逸、沈茲九、陶百川、薩空了、顧執中、蔡楚生、歐陽予倩、諸青來、葉靈鳳和錢俊瑞为执行委员会常务委员。

Subject The Race Renascence Association renamed "The Shanghai Cultural Circles Race Salvation Association." - meeting.
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang. Forwarded by C Crawford

The Race Renascence Association, promoted by the China Literature and Art Society, with an office at Room 631 Continental Emporium Building, Nanking Road, has been renamed "The Shanghai Cultural Circles Race Salvation Association" (上海文化界民族救亡協會).

On July 28 this new organization held an inauguration meeting in the Zang Wen (尚文) Primary School, 50 Yih Lih Rd (一粟街) off Boon Lai Road, Nantao, and passed the following resolutions:-

(2) That the association take part in the activities of the Shanghai Various Circles Enemy-Resisting Support Committee.
(3) That assistance be rendered the Government and the different public bodies in the suppression of smuggled goods.
(4) That a committee be formed to conduct propaganda abroad.
(5) That efforts be made to suppress the activities of traitors.
(6) That the Propaganda Department of the Central Kuomintang be requested to lecture on patriotism.
(7) That local members of the Cultural circles be urged to engage in national salvation propaganda.
(8) That a newspaper be published of the work of the association.

An executive committee of 73 persons was also elected.
The meeting was attended by about 80 persons with Mr. Koo Tseh-tsoong (顧執中) presiding.

Report on state of Central District between 7 a.m. on July 20th 1937,
and 7 a.m.on July 21st 1937 as per instructions from D.O."A" on
July 16th 1937.

Det.Insp. A.Telfer

Sir,

During the period between 7 a.m.on July 20th 1937 and
7 a.m.on July 21st 1937 no report was received of any anti-
Japanese incident in the district in connection with the sino-
Japanese trouble in North China.

Whilst observation was kept on the Continental Emporium
Building, Nanking Road it was noted by C.D.S⁸⁸ Kung Tuh Piau,
36 Soong Yuen Zeu,100 Wong Foh Sung and C.D.C.160 Tseu Tsung
Ching that a meeting was held between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m.on July
20th 1937 at the Shanghai Ant's Club situated at Room No.631.
About twenty local reporters and journalists attended it, but
the nature of it could not be ascertained as it was held behind
closed doors. There was no disturbance and all was orderly.
The president of the meeting it was learned was a reporter
named Tseu Chi Yoong (周志勇). It is suspected the meeting
was held in connection with the fighting in North China.

I am, Sir,
